name: Shelemiah
title: Jeremiah Writes and Sends a Messenger
summary: Shelemiah (also called Shelemiah) was the father of Jehucal (Jukal) and Nethaniah, and served in several roles connected to the prophet Jeremiah and the king's court in Judah. He is mentioned in various contexts in the book of Jeremiah, including as the father of messengers and as one sent to seize the prophet Jeremiah. The name means 'the Lord has repaid' and is borne by several individuals in the Old Testament.

keyEvents.title: Shelemiah's Son Jehucal Sent to Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: King Zedekiah sent Jehucal, son of Shelemiah, to the prophet Jeremiah to ask him to pray to the Lord for the people.

keyEvents.title: Shelemiah Appointed to Seize Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Shelemiah, son of Abdeel, was ordered by King Jehoiakim to seize the prophet Jeremiah and the scribe Baruch, but the Lord hid them.

keyEvents.title: Jehucal Accuses Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Shallum's son Jehucal was among the officials who accused Jeremiah of weakening the people's morale by speaking about Babylon's victory.

keyEvents.title: Irijah, son of Shallum, arrests Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Irijah, son of Shallum and grandson of Hananiah, arrested the prophet Jeremiah at the Benjamin Gate and accused him of intending to defect to the Chaldeans.

keyEvents.title: Shallum as a temple servant after the exile
keyEvents.description: A person named Shallum is also mentioned in connection with the management of the temple supplies after returning from exile under Nehemiah.
